title: Tiled Context Playbook — skim notes, experiment sketches, product hooks
content:
Quick summary:

This is a lightweight playbook of readings + on-paper experiment sketches about 'tiled' or windowed context strategies for long-input LLM workflows. Goal: collect practical takeaways we can test quickly in Redwood's infra and identify a few concrete product hooks for Redwood Optimize and routing policies. Notes are intentionally sloppy — thinking-out-loud for sprint planning.

Motivating problem:
- Users send very long documents (legal, logs, entire webpages) but don't need full-token fidelity across the entire context.
- Naive truncation loses early context; full attention across tens of thousands of tokens is expensive.
- We want heuristics that preserve salient context while keeping latency and cost low.

Skimmed papers/blogs (high-level takeaways):

1) "Adaptive Tile Attention" (preprint; 2026) — idea: split input into tiles and do hierarchical attention where tiles are selectively upgraded based on a lightweight importance scorer.
- Score function can be cheap (tf-idf-ish or shallow LM signal).
- Two-pass pipeline: quick scan -> pick top-k tiles -> full attention on selected tiles plus dense prefix.
- Takeaway: works best when signals are sparse (few tiles matter); overhead of scorer matters.

2) "Selective KV Eviction for Episodic Streams" (conference talk notes)
- Evict entries by recency+importance score; approximate importance via cross-attention energy computed on a sampled minibatch.
- Eviction policy that preserves anchors (named entities, question context) reduces quality drop versus pure LRU.
- Takeaway: combining shallow semantic signals with recency beats naive LRU.

3) "Prefix Tilings for Retrieval-Heavy RAG" (engineering blog + code)
- When retrieval returns many passages, group passages into tiles based on source/document, then do coarse rerank at tile level before token-level scoring.
- Saves expensive cross-attention between query and all retrieval tokens.
- Takeaway: tiling by source + approximate scores is simple and effective.

Why this matters to Redwood:
- Could reduce per-token compute for long-document customers (legal, finance) and improve SLAs for Dedicated customers.
- Natural product hook for Redwood Optimize: suggest tile size / scorer / fallback policies by workload.
- Routing: send quick-scan scorer to cheap capacity tier, escalate high-value tiles to high-performance GPUs.

Experiment sketches (small, actionable):

Exp A — Baseline tiling vs truncation
- Dataset: 2k long documents sampled from internal legal demo set (avg 8k tokens).
- Variants: truncation 2048, tiled quick-scan (tile=512, stride=512), tiled + top-2 selection, tiled + top-4 selection.
- Metrics: answer-F1 (task-specific QA), latency p50/p95, tokens consumed (model billing tokens), model cost per query.
- Hypothesis: top-2 tile selection recovers >85% baseline F1 with <=60% tokens.

Exp B — Cheap scorer cost/benefit curve
- Scorers: tf-idf, small distilled LM (3-parameter prox), cheap classifier trained on small labeled subset.
- Measure scorer CPU time, end-to-end latency, and impact on quality after selection.
- Goal: find the knee where scorer overhead outweighs token savings.

Exp C — Eviction + anchor preservation in streaming chat
- Simulate a 20-turn session appending user history; vary eviction policy: LRU, importance-weighted, anchor-preserve.
- Metric: instruction-following drift (automatic probe prompts) and KL drift on language model logits relative to full-history baseline.

Microbench plan (runtime-level):
- Implement a tiled preprocessor that emits token ranges and scorer output; this lives in a thin layer before the tokenization stage so we can measure early.
- Use existing batcher in serving-runtime with a small shim that expands only selected tiles into attention work.
- Add tracing hooks: scorer-time, tile-selection-time, token-encode-time, model-forward-time per tile.

Measurement definitions (to keep consistent):
- tokens_consumed: model input tokens (after selection) + generation tokens.
- scorer_cpu_ms: wall-time on cheap instance measured per-request.
- quality_delta: relative metric vs full-attend baseline (e.g., F1 or BLEU depending on task).
- cost_estimate_usd: simple conversion using per-GPU-second and per-token token-cost estimates.

Product hooks / suggestions:
- Redwood Optimize rule: "tiled-suggest" — analyze request size distribution and recommend tile size and scorer threshold with expected savings.
- Routing policy: enable two-stage routing for large requests: cheap-scan pool -> upgrade pool for selected tiles. Billing transparency: show scorer costs and net savings in Console.
- Rollout policy: start with a canary threshold (only enable for requests > 3k tokens, < 50KB).

Open questions / risks:
- Interaction with streaming: we need to decide how to reveal partial answers when tiles are selected/processed asynchronously.
- Eval brittleness: some tasks require spread-out context (e.g., referencing an earlier paragraph scattered across tiles). How to detect these?
- Privacy/compliance: if scorer runs outside of private deployment, we must flag PII-sensitive customers; product gating required.
- Quantization/FP16: does tile-based selection amplify quantization artifacts (small context vs big context mismatch)? Need targeted tests.

Notes from internal threads and artifacts:
- Slack: #kv-cache-ops thread had a short convo about anchor policies (Jan-Jun 2026) — link above.
- Related INF ticket: INF-1254 (prototype scorer infra).
- Small PR to runtime (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/3421 — has prototype hooks for selective expansion.

Next steps (actionable):
- 1) Kickoff 1-week spike: implement tile preprocessor + simple tf-idf scorer and run Exp A on 200 docs. Owners: Vikram (lead), Leah (data prep). Due: 2026-08-17.
- 2) Run microbench on Dedicated dev cluster to measure scorer latency and batched behavior. Owner: Omar. Due: 2026-08-21.
- 3) Draft short Redwood Optimize card with suggested UX mock: show suggested tile-size and expected monthly savings for the account. Owner: Vikram + product. Due: 2026-08-28.

TODO (short, quick list):
- [ ] grab 200 long-doc samples from legal-demo dataset (Leah)
- [ ] add tracing counters to batcher shim (Omar)
- [ ] write evaluation script (qa-eval) that compares to full-attend baseline
- [ ] confirm data access constraints for private deployments (security)
- [ ] mock console screenshot for "tiled-suggest" card (UX)

Random heuristics brainstorm (keep):
- Prefer tiles that contain named entities extracted by cheap NER; entities are often anchors for downstream QA.
- If retrieval is present, give retrieval-passage tiles a +boost score by source density.
- For streaming, keep small moving prefix (last 2 turns) always dense and stitch older tiles lazily.

Handy links to read later:
- approximate-importance-scorers.md (local doc, TODO: import)
- blog: fast-tile-attention.org (example code)
- arXiv: adaptive-tile-attention-2026.pdf (downloaded)

End of scratchpad. Notes intentionally rough — will refine into a 1-page PRD if the spike proves promising.

-- Vikram
